profile_text.body:
Microsoft is a public company founded in 1975 and headquartered in Redmond, WA. Its website, in the context captured here, presents Power Automate, a workflow and business process automation product that the company describes as enabling automation across apps, systems, desktop applications, and websites using AI-powered, digital, and robotic process automation. A customer quote on the site describes a data validation process that previously required over 100 people being managed by just a few people after adopting generative AI and Power Automate.

Microsoft tracks a broad portfolio of AI products across multiple categories, including Microsoft Copilot embedded across Microsoft 365, Azure OpenAI Service, Azure Machine Learning, Microsoft Power Automate AI, Microsoft Teams AI, SharePoint AI, Microsoft Designer, Microsoft Clipchamp AI, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, and Microsoft Agent Framework. The Agent Framework is described as the successor to both Semantic Kernel and AutoGen, offering a unified .NET and Python agent SDK with graph workflows and native MCP and A2A support, with Semantic Kernel noted as superseded by it in 2026. Microsoft reported revenue of $331,839,000,000 for the period ending June 30, 2026, and trades on a public exchange under the ticker MSFT with SEC CIK 0000789019.

On the litigation side, Microsoft is a named defendant in The New York Times Co. v. Microsoft Corp. and OpenAI, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, and is also connected to Authors Guild v. OpenAI, Inc., in the same court.
